explanation: Two lines meet at a right angle exactly when their slopes are negative reciprocals: flip one slope over and change its sign. The m slider sets the first line's steepness; the second line is drawn automatically with slope -1/m, so they always cross at 90 degrees. Watch the little corner square stay a perfect right angle no matter how you tilt m, and notice the product m1 * m2 in the readout pins to -1.
bullets: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: m2 = -1 / m1.
The slopes always multiply to -1 (m1 * m2 = -1).
A horizontal line (m = 0) is perpendicular to a vertical line (undefined slope).
